data.name: Pew Pew Party
data.detailed_description:
Welcome to Pew Pew Party – the fast-paced, fun-filled multiplayer FPS where chaos, laughter, and ridiculous shootouts are always on the menu! Whether you’re hopping in for a quick match with friends or grinding your way up the leaderboards, Pew Pew Party is built for pure arcade-style fun. No long tutorials, no waiting around – just grab your blaster, jump into the action, and let the pew pews fly.

Developed and published by Nordôme Studios, Pew Pew Party blends classic arena shooter mechanics with a lighthearted party vibe, making it easy to pick up but hard to put down.

Key Features

  • Fast-Paced Multiplayer Action – Quick rounds keep the energy high, perfect for both casual chaos and competitive play.

  • Colorful Arenas – Jump into vibrant maps designed for maximum fun, from post-apocalyptic arenas to wild playgrounds.

  • Over-the-Top Weapons – From classic rifles to air strikes, everything is designed for fun fights.

  • Party Vibes – Lighthearted style, goofy moments, and non-stop action mean no two matches ever feel the same.

  • Easy to Pick Up, Hard to Master – Simple controls make it accessible, but skillful aim and timing set the sharpshooters apart.

  • Play With Friends – Invite your crew and see who dominates the party, or take the challenge online against the world.

Why You’ll Love It

Pew Pew Party is just another FPS, but it’s a game made for good times. Whether you’re here for friendly trash talk, a quick adrenaline fix, or that perfect trick shot, this is the arena where every match feels like a highlight reel.

Grab your gear, join the fun, and let the party begin – Pew Pew Party is waiting for you!

Trello RoadMap

Pew Pew Party's road map is available by clicking on a button on the main menu in the game.

Message form the developer

Hi, my name is Mikael and I am a Apprentice in automotive mechanic, but I always have been passionate with computers and video games, more specifically: I wanted to make my own game. My only goal with this, is to see people laugh when they play. People enjoy the experience, but at what cost. Nowadays we buy 90$ to play a "New" game that will be not so new the year afterwards. This is the reason why I choose to put mine Free To Play. I don't want people to think that game developers like me steals money from players because it's too expensive. Making a game is one of the most beautiful, risky and time taking experience I have done so far. Thank you!
